title: Equivariant projective Stein constants of a finite cover of a projective scheme
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a projective finite-type $k$-scheme, $X$ a normal integral finite-type $k$-scheme, and $q:X\to S$ a finite $k$-morphism. Put $F=k(X)$ and $e=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, the ring of global regular functions, embedded in $F$ by the generic germ map. Then $e$ is a field finite over $k$ and its image in $F$ is exactly $\{a\in F:a\text{ is algebraic over }k\}$. The canonical evaluation morphism $h:X\to\operatorname{Spec}e$ is proper with geometrically connected fibres. The scheme $X$ is projective over $k$ and over $e$, and is of finite type over $e$. For every separated finite-type $k$-scheme $V$ and every $k$-morphism $f:X\to V$, $f$ admits a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_V$ over $V$ for some $n\geq0$.

If a finite group $J$ acts on $k$ and $X$ compatibly by field and scheme automorphisms, it preserves $e\subset F$, acts there by $j(a)=(j^{-1})^*a$, and makes $h$ equivariant. This action restricts to the given action on $k$. If $l$ is an intermediate field $k\subseteq l\subseteq F$ whose inclusion is supplied by a compatible structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}l$, then this inclusion factors through $e$ and $e/l$ is finite. These assertions do not require faithful group actions.

Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Geometrically connected fibres here mean that $X\times_e E$ is nonempty and connected for every extension field $E/e$. Projective always means a closed immersion in a finite-dimensional projective space over the target. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Schemes, fields, integrality, finite type, finite morphisms, projectivity, properness, function fields, affine spectra, relative algebraic closure, field extensions, geometric connectedness and closed immersions use [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] and [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Tag 03H0, theorem-stein-factorization-Noetherian, over Spec k with normal source; equivariance and constants as in de Jong (1997), Lemma 5.2 proof p.613 and Lemma 5.5 p.614. Projective graph argument: schemes.tex Tag 01KR, lemma-fibre-product-after-map.

proof.text: Write $p:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for the structure map. The one-point affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: its section ring is a field, whose only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$. Apply [lem-fin-finite-over-projective] to $S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the finite map $q$. Its affine-base conclusion gives a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_k$. Thus $p$ is projective, and [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] makes $p$ proper.

source.place: Tags 0B3I (lemma-finite-projective), 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective) and 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper), over the affine base Spec k; affine-base finite-cover conclusion as stated by lem-fin-finite-over-projective.

proof.text: The hypotheses make $X$ integral, separated (by properness), and of finite type over $k$, hence a variety by [def-pc-curve]. Clause (1) of [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety] says that $e=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is a finite field extension of $k$. The generic germ map is injective by [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], so this identifies $e$ with the specified subfield of $F$.

The map $p$ is dominant since $X$ is nonempty and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has one point. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-stein-constant-field] to $p$ (normal integral finite-type source and integral finite-type target). Its chart for the whole affine target identifies its Stein scheme with $\operatorname{Spec}e$ and its first map with evaluation $h$. Therefore $h$ is proper with geometrically connected fibres, and $s:\operatorname{Spec}e\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $k(\operatorname{Spec}e)=\operatorname{Frac}e=e$ and $k(\operatorname{Spec}k)=k$. The evaluation construction has identity pullback on $e$, so its generic-field embedding is precisely the germ embedding of step 2. The constant-field equality in the cited Stein statement consequently gives $e=\{a\in F:a\text{ is algebraic over }k\}$. Its geometric-connectedness conclusion is for all field extensions of the residue field; here the only residue field is $e$. Thus it gives exactly the required nonempty connected $X\times_e E$ for every $E/e$.

source.place: Tag 03H0 (theorem-stein-factorization-Noetherian), properties (1), (2), (4), (5), specialized over Spec k; constant-field identification in lem-sfb-normal-stein-constant-field.

proof.text: The finite map $s$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], hence separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-constant-projective-graph] with its ground field $k$, its finite extension $k/k$, its projective source $X/k$ from step 1, and target $\operatorname{Spec}e$ with map $h$. It gives a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_e$ over $e$. Thus $X$ is projective over $e$. Properness of $h$ from step 3 includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $X/e$ has the required finite-type structure as well.

For the given separated finite-type $V/k$ and $k$-map $f:X\to V$, apply [lem-sfb-finite-constant-projective-graph] again with extension $k/k$, source $X/k$ and target $V$. Its conclusion is the required closed immersion $(i,f):X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^M_k\times_k V\cong\mathbf P^M_V$ over $V$, for some $M\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 01KR (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), separated clause, as assembled in lem-sfb-finite-constant-projective-graph.

proof.text: Write $j_X$ for the automorphism of $X$ associated to $j\in J$. It fixes the unique generic point, so pullback induces a field automorphism of $F$. Pullback sends a global section to a global section and commutes with its generic germ; hence the subfield $e\subset F$ is preserved. Put $\rho_j=(j_X^{-1})^*$ on $F$ and on $e$. Contravariance gives $\rho_{ij}=\rho_i\rho_j$ and $\rho_1=1$, so these are actions. Compatibility of the original structure map says $(j_X^{-1})^*p^*(a)=p^*(j(a))$ for $a\in k$; thus $\rho_j|_k$ is the given field action. On $\operatorname{Spec}e$ take the action $b_j=\operatorname{Spec}(\rho_{j^{-1}})$. By the contravariant functoriality in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $b_{ij}=b_i b_j$. The affine adjunction [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] says that $h$ has pullback the identity on $e$ and determines maps into $\operatorname{Spec}e$ by their global pullback. Both $h\circ j_X$ and $b_j\circ h$ have pullback $j_X^*=\rho_{j^{-1}}:e\to e$; they are equal. This proves equivariance for the very action stipulated in the statement. No injectivity of $J$ into any automorphism group was used.

source.place: Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine), functoriality of pullback and the identity-section evaluation morphism.

proof.text: Let $t:X\to\operatorname{Spec}l$ be the supplied compatible structure map. By [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction], its pullback is a ring map $u:l\to e$ and $t=\operatorname{Spec}(u)\circ h$: the two morphisms have pullback $u$. The generic germ of $u$ is the stipulated inclusion $l\subset F$, so $u$ is injective and its image is that same intermediate field inside $e\subset F$. It respects $k$ by the compatibility assumption. Finally any finite $k$-spanning set of $e$ is also an $l$-spanning set: its $l$-span lies in $e$ and contains its $k$-span, which is all of $e$. Thus $e/l$ is finite, even when $l/k$ was not assumed finite.

source.place: Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine), factorization corresponding to the section-ring map; elementary spanning-set argument.
